---
title: "GeoFetch.jl"
engine: julia
---

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
using GeoFetch, Dates
```

**GeoFetch.jl** builds local [Zarr](https://zarr.dev) stores from remote weather and geoscience datasets. You describe what you want as a small pipeline, and GeoFetch downloads only the pieces it needs and writes them into a single store with labelled dimensions.

## Overview

A pipeline is a chain of stages joined with `|`:

```
Source | Select / Rechunk | Store
```

- **Source** — the upstream dataset and how it is split into fetchable pieces. Presets such as `OISST(...)` and `GFS(...)` build a source for a known dataset.
- **Transform** — `Select` narrows dimensions and variables; `Rechunk` changes the chunk shape of the output.
- **Sink** — `Store` is the Zarr store to write.

Building a pipeline does no I/O, so it can be printed and inspected freely:

```{julia}
pipeline = GFS(start=Date(2026, 11, 8), stop=Date(2026, 11, 8), cycles=[0], steps=[0, 6, 12]) |
    Select(vars=[:t2m, :apcp, :t], level=[850, 500], lon=Between(0, 30), lat=Between(35, 60)) |
    Store("gfs.zarr")
```

`execute` is the one call that downloads data and writes the store:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
execute(pipeline)
```

## Installation

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/RallypointOne/GeoFetch.jl")
```

The registered v0.1.0 predates the pipeline API described here, so install from the repository for now.

## Available sources

| Preset  | Dataset | Access | Auth |
|---------|---------|--------|------|
| `OISST` | NOAA Optimum Interpolation SST v2.1, daily, 0.25° global | NetCDF files over HTTPS (NCEI) | none |
| `GFS`   | NOAA Global Forecast System forecasts, 0.25° / 0.5° / 1° global | GRIB2 messages by byte range (AWS `noaa-gfs-bdp-pds`) | none |
| `ERA5`  | ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis | not implemented yet | — |

### OISST

Daily sea surface temperature on a 0.25° global grid, one NetCDF file (about 1.6 MB) per day. Dimensions are `lon` (0 to 360), `lat`, `zlev` and `time`; variables are `sst`, `anom`, `err` and `ice`.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
pipeline = OISST(start=Date(2025, 1, 1), stop=Date(2025, 1, 3)) |
    Select(vars=:sst, lon=Between(280, 350), lat=Between(20, 60)) |
    Rechunk(time=3) |
    Store("oisst.zarr")

execute(pipeline)
```

### GFS

Global forecasts from the `pgrb2` files of the public AWS bucket, available from 2021-03-23. Dimensions are `lon` (0 to 360), `lat` (north first), `level` (hPa), `step` (lead time in hours) and `time` (forecast initialization).

Each GFS file is about 540 MB at 0.25° and holds several hundred GRIB messages. GeoFetch reads the `.idx` file published next to each one and requests only the byte ranges of the selected variables and levels.

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println("| Variable | Level | Units | Description |")
println("|----------|-------|-------|-------------|")
foreach(GeoFetch._GFS_FIELDS) do f
    lev = occursin("{}", f.level) ? "pressure levels" : f.level
    println("| `", f.name, "` | ", lev, " | ", f.units, " | ", f.long_name, " |")
end
```

Things to know:

- Without a `Select(vars=...)` every variable on every level is fetched, which is about 245 requests and on the order of 1 GB in memory per file at 0.25°.
- A message that a file does not contain is stored as `NaN`. For example `apcp` (precipitation accumulated since forecast start) has no value at step 0.
- At 0.25° every hour up to 120 is available; beyond that, and at 0.5° and 1°, lead times are multiples of 3 up to 384.
- `GFS(...; base=...)` reads from a mirror or a local directory with the same layout as the bucket.

## Selecting and chunking

`Select` takes one keyword per dimension, plus `vars`:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
Select(vars=:sst)                           # one variable
Select(vars=[:t2m, :u10, :v10])             # several
Select(lat=Between(30, 60))                 # closed interval
Select(level=[850, 500])                    # explicit values
Select(time=Date(2025, 1, 1):Day(1):Date(2025, 1, 5))   # a range
```

Selections are applied before anything is downloaded: files outside the selected times are skipped, and unselected variables, levels and grid points are not read.

`Rechunk(time=30)` sets the chunk size of the output store along a dimension. It does not change what is fetched. `Store(path; chunks=Dict(:time => 30))` does the same and takes precedence.

## Reading a store

Stores are plain Zarr and open with any Zarr reader. `Store` writes Zarr v3 by default; pass `zarr_version=2` for v2, and `overwrite=true` to replace an existing store.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Zarr, Dates

g = zopen("gfs.zarr")
t2m = g["t2m"][:, :, :, :]                  # (lon, lat, step, time)
lon = g["lon"][:]
time = DateTime(1970) .+ Second.(g["time"][:])
```

Each dimension is stored as a coordinate array of the same name. Time coordinates are integers with CF `units` attributes: `seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00` for `DateTime` dimensions (GFS) and `days since 1970-01-01` for `Date` dimensions (OISST).

## Examples

The `examples/` directory of the repository has a runnable script per source. Each pulls a small dataset, then reopens the store and prints a summary:

```
julia --project=. examples/oisst.jl
julia --project=. examples/gfs.jl
```
